long_biography.plain_text:
City Centre Deira expressed Majid Al Futtaim's idea that a shopping centre could combine retail with leisure and social life. The development opened in 1995 with Carrefour, Magic Planet and other attractions, establishing a model that the group later carried across the region.

He extended that formula through Mall of the Emirates, where an indoor ski slope turned a retail property into a destination. Al Futtaim also entrusted day-to-day management to non-family executives while retaining control as founder and president. The governance model continued after his death, when his shares passed to successor shareholders through a judicially supervised estate process.

uncertainties.detail: Al Futtaim's historical relationship is unambiguous: he founded the group, beneficially owned almost all its shares and retained control during his lifetime. He died in 2021, and the official 2025 prospectus says those shares were transferred to successor shareholders. The current-relationship contract therefore requires Unknown for this deceased record; Founder remains the strongest historical alternative but is not treated as current.

The successor-owned group continues across retail property, grocery retail, leisure, hotels and communities, but these are no longer Al Futtaim's personal holdings. Diversified is therefore used only as the required origin-sector fallback from his documented creation sectors, not as a claim that the deceased founder currently owns or controls the group.

Associated Press reports that Al Futtaim used funds from the mediated division of the older family business to start his namesake company, while Forbes and official history establish that he separately founded and expanded the new group. Both mechanisms were material, supporting Mixed. The precise settlement assets, legal instruments, chronology and contribution of each mechanism to the eventual fortune remain undisclosed.

Companies House gives the full name Majid Mohammad Al Futtaim and March 1938, matching the immutable record's birth month and year; Dubai legislation uses the transliteration Mohammed. Some secondary profiles instead report 1934 without a precise day. Mohammad is proposed from the directly linked corporate record, the saved 1938 date is left unchanged, and birth day remains blank.

Gulf News reports that Al Futtaim was born in Dubai in the 1930s, consistent with the saved United Arab Emirates birth country. No official civil record or exact birthplace address was found, so the city proposal is high-confidence rather than very-high-confidence.

The dedicated Forbes profile is verified and proposed alongside the official company website. Focused searches did not authenticate any personal LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook or personal website; company accounts were not substituted. Retail real estate and Grocery retail are the minimum active tag set because they capture two independently material wealth engines. Broader commercial-property, leisure, cinema and multi-brand-retail tags would add overlap or overstate secondary operations, so no tag candidates are proposed.
